page: Hetzner Cloud ccx13 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by the QEMU hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC processor configured with 2 vCPUs, which correspond to 1 physical core and 2 threads. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and is equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of an 80 GB NVMe SSD. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance but limited multi-core scaling due to the dual-vCPU configuration. The stress-ng single-core test and Geekbench single-core score both rank in the top 25%, reflecting solid individual thread execution. However, multi-core metrics, such as the Geekbench multi-core score and stress-ng multi-core performance, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the Passmark memory score and small-block read-only memory bandwidth (150.52 GB/sec) are in the bottom 10%, while large-block write bandwidth (26.66 GB/sec) is average. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform moderately, with single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the middle 50%.

Given its hardware profile, the ccx13 server is positioned as a cost-efficient entry point for dedicated CPU resources, avoiding the noisy-neighbor issues of shared-core instances. However, database operations and high-throughput web serving are constrained, as evidenced by a poor Passmark database score and a weak static web serving throughput of 3.1 GB/sec. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, or small-scale development environments that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high memory bandwidth or multi-core parallelization.
